review.reviewer: Claude, maintainer-authorized source and dependency review (AF-CTR-03 delegated author); PR review is recorded separately
review.rationale: AF-CTR-03 part A1a adds accounts, sessions and devices to the Go center behind the dark-deployed identity surface: migration 0002 (the identity and device schemas with their grant, retention and index decisions), the identity core ported from the C# domain rules, passkey registration and sign-in through github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn v0.18.2 (user verification required, ES256 only, attestation none, an advancing signature counter), e-mail codes through a fake or disabled sender, the owner bootstrap by a one-time token whose SHA-256 is deployment configuration, native bearer and browser cookie sessions with refresh rotation and family revocation on reuse, the device list, rate limits per IP prefix and per account kept in PostgreSQL, audit records on the platform chain, and an operation table that serves exactly the A1a methods of IdentityService and DeviceService and leaves every other method unregistered (fail closed). The Worker answers a disabled surface with STATE/not_activated and a rate-limited identity call with RESOURCE/rate_limited without waking the Container; production enables no new surface and the acceptance environment enables identity. The linked closure of go-webauthn (twelve modules: go-webauthn/x, fxamacker/cbor, x448/float16, golang-jwt/jwt, google/go-tpm, google/uuid, go-viper/mapstructure, tinylib/msgp, philhofer/fwd, golang.org/x/crypto and golang.org/x/sys) is admitted with complete licences under go-<name>-legal-r1 records and shipped in the image notices; the Contracts Go module moves to v1.0.0-ci.416.1 (Contracts #121, 62ccef1) under go-contractsgo-legal-r2. No npm or NuGet package, base image or toolchain changes. The C# Native AOT executable stays the image default for the Hello rollback and the retained D1 gate.
